extracted.intended_audience: Congress, NSF policymakers, NSF program managers, and the research community (applicants and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for how the National Science Foundation should conduct and monitor peer review of research proposals, including methods of review, confidentiality, appeals, reviewer selection, and support for innovation and young scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select for scientific quality and prospect of benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review process is used to select for funding those projects offering both the highest quality of science and the greatest prospect for resultant benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should weigh intrinsic scientific merit and potential benefits; this is the core purpose driving all review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness, objectivity, freedom from bias, fairness and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review process should be open, objective, and free from bias; the research community must perceive the process to be fair, equitable, and accessible to all qualified persons--both as research applicants and as reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perception of fairness is as important as procedural fairness. Policies and publications (e.g., reviewer listings, Grant Policy Manual) should help inform the community and improve perceived objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve peer evaluation of intrinsic scientific merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review should continue to preserve the traditional benefits of peer evaluation of intrinsic scientific merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain reviewer focus on scientific quality rather than purely administrative or non-scientific criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary method selection per program
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Foundation program must select a 'primary method' for peer review as the minimum review to be accorded all proposals in that program (ad hoc mail review, panel review, or a combination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary method can be supplemented with additional reviews, site visits, or other appraisal methods as needed; choice should reflect program needs and disciplinary traditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announce primary method and evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: '. . .the primary method of peer review in each program, including the evaluation criteria reviewers are requested to consider in reviewing proposals, shall be suitably announced.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs must publicly state both the review mechanism and the criteria reviewers will use so applicants understand how proposals will be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a mix of review forms appropriate to the discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: No single system (panel, individual mail, or combination) is adequate for the diverse set of NSF programs; method should match the nature of proposals (e.g., panels for homogeneous or interdisciplinary work; ad hoc for specialized knowledge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imposing uniformity; allow program managers discretion to choose the best-suited method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ad hoc mail review procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: For ad hoc mail review, the program manager selects 3 to 10 reviewers deemed qualified; reviewers are sent the proposal, reviewing forms, and general criteria and asked for (1) an objective evaluation (from excellent to poor) and (2) written comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ad hoc reviewers provide access to specialized expertise not available on panels; selection must follow program policies and Board resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel review uses assembled panels (5 to 12 individuals) who receive proposal packages in advance, consider mail reviews, compare assessments in meetings, and issue overall panel recommendations; primary reviewers may be assigned when proposal volume is large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels are effective when interaction among experts is required (e.g., interdisciplinary proposals); any panel member may review any proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory groups do not review individual proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory groups/panels are used to determine program balance and define scientific priorities; they do not review individual proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep advisory roles distinct from proposal-evaluation roles to avoid conflicts and role confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program manager and multi-level decision accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether by individual reviewers or a combined review, the NSF program manager makes the recommendation to fund or not; that recommendation is reviewed by section head, Division Director, sometimes Directorate Assistant Director, and an Action Review Board external to the specific program area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear lines of responsibility; program managers rely heavily on peer evaluations but retain final recommendation authority subject to internal review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection, broad cadre and updating
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts are made to utilize the broadest possible cadre of reviewers and panelists; the list of qualified reviewers is updated continually; membership on advisory panels is limited to 2- or 3-year terms; advisory committee members are appointed by the Assistant Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continually refresh reviewer pools to broaden representation and expertise; limit panel tenure to avoid ossification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer counts per proposal tailored by directorate
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of reviewers per proposal varies by directorate (e.g., MPE avg 4.2, STIA and interdisciplinary areas require more); adjust reviewer counts to fit proposal complexity and interdisciplinarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use more reviewers for interdisciplinary or complex proposals; document typical reviewer counts by program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of reviewers' names and verbatim comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide applicants reviewers' comments verbatim but preserve the anonymity of reviewers (delete names and identifying data). The Board believes unsigned verbatim comments strike the best available balance between confidentiality and information to applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid releasing signed comments; maintain anonymity to secure candid evaluations; changes to confidentiality should be made slowly, if at all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of list of reviewers (aggregated) annually
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF will publish the listing of peer reviewers used by NSF divisions (names and institutional affiliations) aggregated by directorate annually to provide the research community with information regarding the reviewer base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication should be aggregated by directorate rather than in a more detailed form unless careful study supports less aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide applicants basis for adverse actions and opportunity to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request, the program director must show cause for an adverse action by providing the applicant with information concerning the basis for NSF action including, when requested, verbatim comments of the peer reviews (with identifying data deleted). The program director must afford the applicant an opportunity to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about basis for decisions is required; applicants should be able to correct misunderstandings or supply rebuttals before higher-level reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal reconsideration/appeals procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal procedure (instituted Jan 27, 1976) allows applicants to request reconsideration: first to assistant director, and, failing resolution, the applicant's home institution may request reconsideration by the Deputy Director of the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are internal, multi-level, and require written requests; track and report numbers of appeals by program area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberal resubmission policy as part of effective peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: A liberal 'resubmissions' policy is an important adjunct to the review procedure; effective peer review makes use of and encourages resubmission, with reviewers assisting colleagues to improve proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage applicants to revise and resubmit based on reviewers' technical comments; view feedback as integral to strengthening proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation policy for reviewers and panelists
rubrics_metrics.description: Ad hoc reviewers are not compensated financially. Most research panel members and site visitors receive a modest daily honorarium and travel allowances; science education one-time panels receive travel compensation only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize participation as professional responsibility but provide modest compensation for panel service to offset costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand reviewer base to include 4-year college faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an extensive list of qualified individuals in 4-year colleges willing to review proposals and serve on panels, and administrative procedures to monitor utilization of reviewers from 4-year colleges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively recruit and monitor inclusion of faculty from undergraduate institutions to ensure broader representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and study effects of confidentiality and reviewer/publication practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect further information concerning effects on the peer review system of the level of confidentiality in which peer reviewers' names and verbatim comments are held; study the effects of publishing reviewer lists in different forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct empirical studies (e.g., NAS blind-review experiments, internal analyses) before altering confidentiality practices; proceed cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study blind review (removing proposer identity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation asked the NAS to conduct an experiment comparing usual peer review, NAS panel review, and mail review with proposers' names and institutions removed to determine differences arising from anonymous proposers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use experimental evidence to evaluate potential bias and the desirability/feasibility of reviewer blinding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor reviewer–proposer similarity effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal NSF studies (e.g., 75,000 reviews) found little relationship between ratings and locations or academic status similarity between proposers and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use statistical monitoring to detect favoritism or systematic bias; communicate findings to the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor program- and field-level trends and mismatch issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish internal programs (Planning Environment Review, Science Resources Studies, Science Indicators, State of Academic Science studies) to monitor mismatch between the size of the scientific community and available funds and to develop indicators of trouble spots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link monitoring results to long-range planning and budgeting processes and use outside reviews of principal research activities to assess program decisionmaking under limited resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for innovative research must be assessed and tracked
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the Foundation's role in funding innovations (retrospective analyses of significant advances, percentage of NSF support for identified innovations) and assess adequacy of decision-making procedures for finding and funding innovative research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that many significant advances arise unexpectedly or from general research lines rather than explicit targeted proposals; tailor programs to encourage high-risk/high-reward work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for young scientists requires targeted, case-by-case effort
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability of young scientists to secure research support varies by discipline; specialized NSF efforts (e.g., Cellular Biology Program) have been successful but indicate case-by-case development is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement programs and selection practices that help establish promising young scientists, recognizing discipline-specific needs and competitive pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable support for undergraduate-teaching institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many college faculty are capable of highly productive research; success ratio of awards to applications is about the same among all types of institutions; increase use of college faculty as reviewers/advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide administrative support and reviewer inclusion to ensure fair access for investigators at primarily undergraduate institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping, transparency and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF should provide the Board specific information regarding the names and organizational affiliations of proposers used and the numbers of formal appeals initiated in each program area; Grant Policy Manual published in Federal Register and copies available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and share statistics necessary for oversight, planning, and public understanding of peer review operations.
